html:
The founding of the People's Republic of China, announced by Mao Zedong, chairman of the Chinese Communist Party, from the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Tiananmen Square, Beijing, on 1 October 1949.

It came at the end of the Chinese Civil War. The Communists and Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists had fought on and off since 1927, with a truce against Japan. After Japan's surrender in 1945 the war resumed in full. By 1949 Communist armies had taken the north and crossed the Yangtze. Chiang's government was falling back to the south and then to Taiwan, where it went into exile in December.

At the ceremony Mao announced the new Central People's Government, the new flag with five stars was raised and troops paraded. The Communists had earlier set up a Chinese Soviet Republic in the areas they held in the 1930s, but this was the founding of a state for the whole mainland. Days before, Mao had told a conference that the Chinese people had stood up, after a century of foreign attacks that began with the First Opium War.

The date is China's National Day, marked each year with a week's holiday. What followed was the era of the People's Republic, first under Mao and then under the reformers.
sum: The founding of the People's Republic of China, announced by Mao Zedong, chairman of the Chinese Communist Party, from the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Tiananmen Square, Beijing, on 1 October 1949.
